title: Engineering Scalable Distributed Services for Real-Time Big Data Analytics
display_name: Engineering Scalable Distributed Services for Real-Time Big Data Analytics
abstract: There is high demand for tools that analyze large sets of streaming data in both industrial and academic settings. While existing work has examined a wide range of issues, we focus on query support. In particular, we focus on providing analysts flexibility with respect to the types of queries they can make on large data sets in real time as well as over historical data. We have designed and implemented a lightweight service-based framework-EPIC Real-Time-that manages a set of queries that can be applied to user-initiated data analysis events (such as studying tweets generated during a disaster). Our prototype combines stream processing and batch processing techniques inspired by the Lambda Architecture. We investigate a core set of query types that can answer a wide range of queries asked by analysts who study crisis events. In this paper, we present a prototype implementation of EPIC Real-Time which makes use of event-driven and reactive programming techniques. We also present a performance evaluation on how efficiently the real-time and batch-oriented queries perform, how well these queries meet the needs of our analysts, and provide insight into how EPIC Real-Time performs along a number of dimensions including performance, usability, scalability, and reliability.

title: Playing with Fire: Assessing the effects of risk interdependency, social norms, and costs on homeowners’ wildfire mitigation decisions using choice experiments
display_name: Playing with Fire: Assessing the effects of risk interdependency, social norms, and costs on homeowners’ wildfire mitigation decisions using choice experiments
abstract: This data set emerges from an online choice experiments with homeowners in areas at risk of wildfire in Western Colorado to assess the role of social interactions in shaping wildfire mitigation decisions. These experiments manipulated conditions on neighboring properties to separately identify two social effect pathways: 1) risk interdependency, or the effect of neighbors' vegetation conditions on an individual's own perceived risk and subsequent actions, and 2) social norms, or the desire to conform to dominant behaviors in one's reference group.

title: Tensile Strength of a Self-gravitating Granular Bridge
display_name: Tensile Strength of a Self-gravitating Granular Bridge
abstract: This is the complete data obtained from the simulations done to measure the tensile strength of self-gravitating rebolith. In these simulations, small spherical and polihedral coheisve particles are placed in between two, 1m spherical "boulders". All systems are let to accrete gravitationally first and once accretion is finished, the boulders are pulled apart until the bridge, formed by the small particles (regolith), breaks in tension. The pulling force is incremented by 2% of the total gravitational attraction between the two boulders every 5 seconds. The regolith particles vary in size, from 5cm to 2cm; additionally, the polyhedral particles vary their axis ratios from 0.4 to 1.0. The simulations were carried out to understand how tensile strength changes with particle shape and particle size. Simulation scripts and input files, as well as analysis scripts are part of the data set. The Python scripts used to run the simulations can be found at https://github.com/dpsanchez/GranularBridge. LMGC90 is an open source code that can be freely downloaded from https://git-xen.lmgc.univ-montp2.fr/lmgc90/lmgc90_user/-/wikis/home. The Mathematica scripts to compile the processed data have also been included here. The script for spherical particles has to run first and then the script for polyhedral particles, but you have to change the home directory (SetDirectory[]) This study was carried out as part of the Sample Analysis Test of the sample brought from asteroid Bennu by the OSIRIS-REx mission. The publication making use of these data should be puclished by Nature Communications and has the title: "A Universal Scaling Framework for Granular Asteroid Strength and its Application to Bennu's Surface", Sánchez, P et al.

title: SORCE-SIM Spectral Solar Irradiance Level 3 ENIGMA (L3E)
display_name: SORCE-SIM Spectral Solar Irradiance Level 3 ENIGMA (L3E)
abstract: The SORCE-SIM Solar Spectral Irradiance (SSI) data products are provided on a fixed wavelength scale which varies in spectral resolution from 1-34 nm over the entire spectral range. Irradiances are reported at a mean solar distance of 1 AU and zero relative line-of-sight velocity with respect to the Sun. Version 28 SORCE-SIM data product is the result of the NASA Solar Irradiance Science Team (SIST) ENIGMA project. It incorporates updated solar exposure records and degradation corrections based on the delay between solar observations when compared to the NNLSSI proxy model. A new absolute calibration was applied to the IRRADIANCES, based on the TSIS-1 SIM measurememnts during the overlap period of the two missions. The details of this effort are included in the release notes available with the dataset and at https://lasp.colorado.edu/ SORCE-SIM Solar Spectral Irradiance (SSI) Measurement Summary. Measuring Instrument SIM (Spectral Irradiance Monitor) Temporal Cadence Daily Detector Radiometer (ESR) and Photodiodes (UV, VIS, & IR) Instrument Modes 31 (ESR), 41 (VIS), 43 (UV), 44 (IR) Spectral Range 210.04-2401.40 nm Spectral Resolution variable (1-34 nm) Accuracy 2% Long-Term Repeatability < 0.1%/yr The dataset is provided in netCDF4 and IDL Savefile formats. Each include a descriptive header of the content. Each data record contains the nominal date in YYYYMMDD.D and Julian Day Number (JDN), the wavelength of the irradiance measurement (repeated in the MIN_WAVELENGTH and MAX_WAVELENGTH fields), the INSTRUMENT_MODE, DATA_VERSION, spectral IRRADIANCE, IRRADIANCE_UNCERTAINTY, and data QUALITY flag.

title: Supporting data for "Vegetation-fire feedback reduces projected area burned under climate change"
display_name: Supporting data for "Vegetation-fire feedback reduces projected area burned under climate change"
abstract: Climate influences vegetation directly and through climate-mediated disturbance processes, such as wildfire. Temperature and area burned are positively associated, conditional on availability of vegetation to burn. Fire is a self-limiting process that is influenced by productivity. Yet, many fire projections assume sufficient vegetation to support fire, with substantial implications for carbon (C) dynamics and emissions. We simulated forest dynamics under projected climate and wildfire for the Sierra Nevada, accounting for climate effects on fuel flammability (static) and climate and prior fire effects on fuel availability and flammability (dynamic). We show that compared to climate effects on flammability alone, accounting for the interaction of prior fires and climate on fuel availability and flammability moderates the projected increase in area burned by 14.3%. This reduces predicted increases in area-weighted median cumulative emissions by 38.3 Tg carbon dioxide (CO2) and 0.6 Tg particulate matter (PM1), or 12.9% and 11.5%, respectively. Our results demonstrate that after correcting for potential over-estimates of the effects of climate-driven increases in area burned, California is likely to continue facing significant wildfire and air quality challenges with on-going climate change.

title: Temporal reformatting of odor signals by flow environments: CFD dataset
display_name: Temporal reformatting of odor signals by flow environments: CFD dataset
abstract: This dataset contains the raw data to accompany the paper "Temporal reformatting of odor signals by flow environments" by Stark et al., 2026. These data are derived from 2D computational fluid dynamics simulations in a rectangular domain in which an odor source at (0, 0) releases passive scalars isokinetically into a chaotic flow generated by non-zero mean flow through an array of cylinders of varying sizes. The resultant data consist of all 2D fluid velocity components (u = x-velocity and v = y-velocity) and the passive scalar concentration field resulting from the advection, mixing, and diffusion of the odorant released into the flow. The paper results and figures utilize the data in the folders "Flow Data" and "Odor Data." The folder "Model_verification_t180to360s" contains three additional minutes of simulation data that was used for verification of statistical convergence of the model results.

title: Data for Continuous recoil-driven lasing and cavity frequency pinning with laser-cooled atoms
display_name: Data for Continuous recoil-driven lasing and cavity frequency pinning with laser-cooled atoms
abstract: Laser-cooled gases of atoms interacting with the field of an optical cavity are a versatile tool for quantum sensing and the simulation of quantum systems. These systems can exhibit phenomena such as self-organization phase transitions, lasing mechanisms, squeezed states, and protection of quantum coherence. However, investigations of these phenomena typically occur in a discontinuous manner due to the need to reload atomic ensembles. Here we demonstrate hours-long continuous lasing from laser-cooled 88Sr atoms loaded into a ring cavity. The required inversion to produce lasing arises from inversion in the atomic momentum degrees of freedom, which is linked to the self-organization phase transitions and collective atomic recoil lasing observed previously only in a cyclic fashion. We find that over a broad parameter range, the sensitivity of the lasing frequency to changes in cavity frequency is significantly reduced due to an atomic loss mechanism, suggesting a potential approach for mitigating low-frequency cavity noise. Our findings open opportunities for continuous cavity QED experiments and robust and continuous superradiant lasers.

title: FIRED FINLAND
display_name: FIRED FINLAND
abstract: This is event- and daily-level polygons for the Fire event delineation (FIRED) product for Finland from November 2001 to January 2022. It is derived from the MODIS MCD64A1 burned area product (see https://lpdaac.usgs.gov/products/mcd64a1v006/ for more details). The MCD64A1 is a monthly raster grid of estimated burned dates. Firedpy (www.github.com/earthlab/firedpy) is an algorithm that converts these rasters into events by stacking the entire time series into a spatial-temporal data cube, then uses an algorithm to assign event identification numbers to pixels that fit into the same 3-dimensional spatial temporal window. This particular dataset was created using a spatial parameter of 5 pixels and 11 days. The primary benefit to this dataset over others is the ability to calculate fire spread rate. For each of these products (events and daily) the event identification numbers are the same, but the event-level product has only single polygons for each entire event, while the daily product has separate polygons for each date per event.

title: Single-turnover kinetics of BAM activity with bOmpA-A488
display_name: Single-turnover kinetics of BAM activity with bOmpA-A488
abstract: The B-barrel assembly machine is an essential, multiprotein complex that folds and inserts outer membrane proteins (OMPs) into the outer membrane of Gram-negative bacteria. The BAM complex is composed of the essential BamA OMP, which contains a transmembrane B-barrel domain and five periplasmic polypeptide transport-associated (POTRA) domains in E. coli. The BamA POTRA domains scaffold the essential lipoprotein BamD and the nonessential lipoproteins BamBCE. While an abundance of cell-based phenotypic assays and structural data have elucidated important insight into BAM-catalyzed OMP folding, methods for quantitative analysis of BAM function have been challenging. We use a quantitative fluorescent reporter of OMP folding, bOmpA-A488, to obtain single-turnover kinetic parameters for wild-type BAM complex in vitro, which agree well with estimates necessary for BAM function in vivo. Our fluorescence-based single-turnover activity assay was further used to investigate the roles of the lipoproteins and the POTRA domains 1-3 on BAM activity. The data file provided includes relevant raw data for SDS-PAGE densitometry, fluorescence measurements, and circular dichroism measurements.

title: Putting the ‘I’ Back in BIPOC: Indigenous-Specific Inclusion Initiatives across Academic Libraries in the United States and Canada Dataset
display_name: Putting the ‘I’ Back in BIPOC: Indigenous-Specific Inclusion Initiatives across Academic Libraries in the United States and Canada Dataset
abstract: This dataset examines academic libraries’ resources and services specifically centering Indigenous patrons and Indigenous Knowledge, as well as targeted support for Critical Indigenous Studies (CIS) academic programs at colleges and universities across the United States and Canada. In addition to a comprehensive assessment of Indigenous-specific liaison librarians and libguides, this overview investigates correlations between additional overlapping factors including: Indigenous Studies curricular offerings, institutional land acknowledgements, research output, institutional distinction as Title III Minority Serving Institutions (MSI), and membership in collegiate associations such as the Association of American Universities (AAU), Association of Public and Land-grant Universities (APLU), and National Collegiate Athletics Association Division I Football Bowl Subdivision (NCAA FBS). As a result, this dataset provides multiple points of comparison which serves to outline a more thorough illustration of the academic environments in which college and university libraries operate. Moreover, this constellation of data points serves to demonstrate both the academic libraries concentrating their efforts to support Indigenous members of their respective campus communities, as well as how they align these efforts with broader campus initiatives.

title: Regina Tornado Scenario Windspeed Maps
display_name: Regina Tornado Scenario Windspeed Maps
abstract: The maps presented here describe a hypothetical but realistic tornado striking Regina, Saskatchewan. The scenario tornado reaches a maximum rating of EF4 on the Enhanced Fujita scale. It resembles the Regina tornado of Sunday, June 30, 1912. The scenario tornado has a similar path and damage swath, approximately 43 kilometres long and up to 400 metres wide as it passes through downtown Regina. The scenario tornado produces wind speeds reaching 86 m/s (310 km/h). This technical memo develops a plausible wind speed map. The map is available as images here and in electronic formats for later use. The map is consistent with first-hand observations from 1912 and comports with the current state of the art in tornado climatology. Severe rain and hail could accompany such a tornado. Wind speed map colors reflect bands of 3-second peak gust velocity that align with the Enhanced Fujita (EF) scale. White means 25-37 m/s (EF0). Green means 38-49 m/s (EF1). Yellow reflects 50-61 m/s (EF2). Red means 62-74 m/s (EF3). Burnt (hex color #74021a) reflects 75-86 m/s (EF4).

title: TSIS-1 SIM L3 V13 Solar Spectral Irradiance
display_name: TSIS-1 SIM L3 V13 Solar Spectral Irradiance
abstract: NASA’s Total and Spectral Solar Irradiance Sensor-1 (TSIS-1) operates on the International Space Station. TSIS-1 provides absolute measurements of the total solar irradiance (TSI) and spectral solar irradiance (SSI), important for accurate scientific models of climate change and solar variability. TSIS-1 is comprised of two instruments, the Total Irradiance Monitor (TIM), and the Spectral Irradiance Monitor (SIM). This repository archives Version 13 (V13) of the TSIS-1 SIM Level 3 (L3) data release, and contains SSI in two cadences, 12-hour, and 24-hour. The TSIS-1 SIM L3 V13 data release contains data from 2018-03-14 to 2025-09-16. Version 13 (V13) addresses data issues resulting from anomalies in the TSIS-1 SIM Digital Signal Processor (DSP) and the Electrical Substitution Radiometers (ESRs) that occurred in September and October 2024. The SIM DSP stopped responding to ground commands on September 4, 2023, and command and control were restored on October 21, 2023. Post-anomaly checkout revealed changes in ESR responsivity for certain configurations and wavelength ranges. Data affected in these ESR wavelength regions are corrected and first published in V13. The TSIS-1 SIM ESRs are used directly for all reported solar spectral irradiances (SSIs) at wavelengths longer than 1620 nm. Prior to V13, ESR data were also used as the irradiance reference for diode measurements between 408 and 1620 nm. V13 addresses the ESR anomaly in two key ways: (1) ESR data collected after the anomaly are no longer used to correct diode degradation in the 408–1620 nm range, and a diode degradation model is used instead; and (2) for all SSIs longer than 1620 nm after September 4, 2023, a wavelength-dependent spectral correction is applied to the measured ESR irradiances. As a consequence of the DSP anomaly, the Channel-C scans scheduled for October 2023 were not performed. However, Channel-C scans were successfully completed in April 2024 and October 2024. Degradation correction updates in V13 incorporate updated Channel-C diode data from the April 2023, April 2024, and October 2024 calibration campaigns, which were not included in V12. The exact relationship between the DSP and ESR anomalies remains unclear, as ESR telemetry did not exhibit anomalous behavior until after SIM was power cycled on October 21, 2023. Following the ESR anomaly, the SIM ESRs exhibited wavelength- and channel-pairing-dependent changes. For the A_B and B_A channel pairings, these manifest as static offset changes, while the Channel-C ESR exhibits a time-dependent behavior. A minor re-release of V13 was issued on September 3, 2025, to improve wavelength alignment in SIM V13 data products. Following the initial V13 release in January 2025, the thermal pointing system began exhibiting more frequent pointing excursions near zero crossings. These excursions reduced the algorithm’s ability to accurately determine spectral wavelength alignment, with the most pronounced effects observed in the 800–950 nm range and near 400 nm. As a result, data collected after the ESR anomaly were reprocessed to improve wavelength alignment in the final V13 data products. See the release notes TSIS_SIM_V13_Release_Notes_V2.pdf or the TSIS SIM Data Products Release Notes page (https://lasp.colorado.edu/tsis/data/ssi-data/sim-ssi-release-notes/) for further details, and instructions for obtaining the latest TSIS-1 SIM L3 data release. Data is archived in ASCII, netCDF, and IDL SAVfile format.

title: FIRED Argentina (s5/t3, s8/t3) Nov 2000 - July 2024
display_name: FIRED Argentina (s5/t3, s8/t3) Nov 2000 - July 2024
abstract: This is event- and daily-level polygons for the fire event delineation (FIRED) product for ARGENTINA from November 2000 to December 2024. It is derived from the MODIS MCD64A1 burned area product (see https://lpdaac.usgs.gov/products/mcd64a1v061/ for more details). The MCD64A1 is a monthly raster grid of estimated burned dates. Firedpy (https://github.com/earthlab/firedpy) is an algorithm that converts these rasters into events by stacking the entire time series into a spatial-temporal data cube, then uses an algorithm to assign event identification numbers to pixels that fit into the same 3-dimensional spatial temporal window. This particular pair of datasets were created using a spatial parameters of 5 pixels and 3 days, and 8 pixels and 3 days. Daily polygons are included and the event identification numbers are the same for both files, but the event-level product has only single polygons for each entire event, while the daily product has separate polygons for each date per event. See the associated paper for more details on the methods and more: Balch, J.K.; St. Denis, L.A.; Mahood, A.L.; Mietkiewicz, N.P.; Williams, T.M.; McGlinchy, J.; Cook, M.C. FIRED (Fire Events Delineation): An Open, Flexible Algorithm and Database of US Fire Events Derived from the MODIS Burned Area Product (2001–2019). Remote Sens. 2020, 12, 3498.

title: Range-Wide North American Freshwater Mussels (Unionidae, Ambleminae) 2D and 3D Morphometric Datasets
display_name: Range-Wide North American Freshwater Mussels (Unionidae, Ambleminae) 2D and 3D Morphometric Datasets
abstract: This dataset submission provides two complementary morphometric datasets—2D linear and 3D volumetric—generated to investigate shell variation and resource allocation in freshwater mussels (Subfamily: Ambleminae) across environmental gradients within eight major U.S. water resource regions in North America. The 2D dataset comprises linear measurements for 1,169 specimens across 10 species representing three tribes: Lampsilini (Cyprogenia stegaria, Dromus dromas, Obliquaria reflexa, Obovaria subtrotunda), Pleurobemini (Fusconaia flava, Fusconaia subrotunda, Pleurobasus cooperianus), and Quadrulini (Pustulosa pustulosa, Theliderma metanevra, Quadrula quadrula). Specimens were sourced from four major natural history collections (USNM, UMMZ, WNHC, and ANSP). Data includes specimen information, linear shell measurements (length, width, and inflation) as well as calculated inflation indices to assess morphological response to river flow. The 3D Volumetric Dataset focuses on 110 specimens of Fusconaia subtrotunda (smooth-shelled) and Pustulosa pustulosa (sculptured). Models were generated via structured light scanning at 0.05 mm resolution (Artec Space Spider). All specimens in both datasets have locality and collecting event metadata included, are georeferenced and contained National Hydrography Dataset Plus (NHDPlusV2)-derived COMID, annual mean river flow rates, and HUC levels (HUC2 to HUC12). These datasets serve as a high-resolution resource for evolutionary biologists and malacologists exploring the intersection of shell plasticity, hydrology, and functional tradeoffs.

title: Amazon Fires Data
display_name: Amazon Fires Data
abstract: Slash-and-burn agricultural practices have led to deforestation across large sections of the Amazon rain forest. This practice and other natural biomass burning emits carbonaceous aerosols that negatively impact human health by increasing fine particulate matter (PM2.5) exposure. These negative health impacts are in addition to detrimental climatological and ecological impacts. We estimate PM2.5-related premature deaths in Brazil associated with this burning, focusing on temporal, interannual and spatial trends. We find that in 2019, 2200 (1700, 2710) premature deaths were attributable to fire emissions making up 4.3% (3.3%, 5.3%) of all PM2.5-related premature deaths in Brazil. Most of these premature deaths were attributable to ischemic heart disease (IHD) and acute lower respiratory illness (ALRI). Fire emissions from 2019 contributed 75.4% (5.7%, 181.2%) more premature deaths than in 2018. Biomass burning emissions from throughout Brazil contribute significantly to premature deaths, with the largest burning events occurring in the north-western region. The impact of fires on PM2.5-related premature deaths is highest in heavily populated regions despite their fires being one to two orders of magnitude smaller than the largest burning events. In 2019, premature death contributions increased in most densely populated regions with minor decreases occurring near Sao Paulo.

title: Community Aerosol and Radiation Model for Atmospheres (CARMA) standalone 4.11 code
display_name: Community Aerosol and Radiation Model for Atmospheres (CARMA) standalone 4.11 code
abstract: CARMA is a general-purpose sectional microphysics code that has been used to study a wide variety of aerosols in planetary atmospheres. It originated from a one-dimensional stratospheric aerosol code developed by Turco et al. (1979) and Toon et al. (1979) that included both gas-phase sulfur chemistry and aerosol microphysics. The model was improved and extended to three dimensions as described by Toon et al. (1988). CARMA has been applied to almost every cloud and aerosol on Earth, as well as those on Venus, Mars, Titan, and exoplanets. This is the standalone CARMA version 4.11. To get the latest code, please download from https://github.com/ESCOMP/CARMA_base.

title: Modeling of GUV222-driven increases in SOA concentrations in an unoccupied office
display_name: Modeling of GUV222-driven increases in SOA concentrations in an unoccupied office
abstract: This data set contains the data for the paper "Modeling of GUV222-driven increases in SOA concentrations in an unoccupied office". An abstract for the paper is as follows: The COVID-19 pandemic led to high interest in germicidal ultraviolet (GUV) lamps, which can deactivate bacteria and viruses in infectious aerosols. Recently, lamps using 222 nm (GUV222) light to disinfect occupied spaces have become more popular and available, as the wavelength is safer for human exposure than 254 nm lamps. However, GUV222 produces ozone, which drives the formation of other pollutants. Previous work in a controlled environmental Teflon chamber with GUV222 has shown significant production of ozone followed by the formation of secondary organic aerosol (SOA) from limonene ozonolysis and developed a model of this process. This work adapts that model for use in an unoccupied office and shows it is able to accurately predict SOA formation and yield given a continuous source of limonene. SOA yields from limonene in the office were found to be similar to those measured in a Teflon chamber. However, SOA formation resulting from briefly emitted limonene was harder to capture in the model. Number concentrations of ultrafine particles increased under GUV222 after limonene injection while overall SOA mass concentrations had negligible change. GUV222 also had other impacts on room chemistry; concentrations of most VOCs measured increased under GUV222, driven by gas and surface phase ozone reactions, as well as potentially direct surface emissions.

title: Evolution of N-terminal mechanical lability as a determinant for Type III Secretion
display_name: Evolution of N-terminal mechanical lability as a determinant for Type III Secretion
abstract: Many Gram-negative pathogens critically depend on the Type III secretion system (T3SS) to inject effector proteins into host cells for colonization. Because the channel of the T3SS is narrow (~2 nm), effectors must be unfolded for secretion. However, the T3SS cannot unfold mechanically robust substrates (GFP, ubiquitin, and dihydrofolate reductase), severely impairing their secretion. Consistent with this, effectors are exceptionally mechanically labile, unfolding at low forces. Thus, secretion competency is correlated with mechanical properties. Effector sequences have significantly diverged from non-effectors, suggesting that secretion exerts evolutionary pressure selecting mechanical lability. Here, using atomic-force-microscopy–based force spectroscopy, we show that effector NleC is mechanically labile (Funfold = 13.5 pN at 100 nm/s) and mechanically compliant, as characterized by a large distance to the transition state (Δx‡ = 2.7 nm). In contrast, the non-effector homolog protealysin is mechanically stable (Funfold = 50.7 pN at 100 nm/s) and brittle (Δx‡ = 0.7 nm), comparable to proteins known to impair secretion (Funfold > 80 pN; Δx‡ < 0.4 nm). Denaturant-induced unfolding assays demonstrate that effectors exhibit rates typical of their fold, further reinforcing mechanical properties rather than fast unfolding kinetics (k0) predicts secretion. Steered molecular dynamic simulations revealed NleC unfolding initiates at the N-terminus, consistent with current secretion models, whereas protealysin unfolding initiates at the C-terminus. Notably, the NleC N-terminus is primarily α-helical while non-effector homologs contain β-sheets, which may account for the distinct unfolding pathway. title: Multi-Seasonal, Multimodal Field-Robotics Data for Ecological Monitoring of Degraded Rangelands
display_name: Multi-Seasonal, Multimodal Field-Robotics Data for Ecological Monitoring of Degraded Rangelands
abstract: The Canyonlands Dataset is a large-scale, multi-seasonal, multimodal field-robotics dataset for research on autonomous ecological monitoring and restoration of degraded rangelands. Data were gathered with a teleoperated Clearpath Husky ground robot across two field campaigns: May 2022 (early germination) and November 2022 (seed stage), at the Canyonlands Research Center near Monticello, in southeastern Utah, revisiting the same eighteen 10 m x 10 m experimental plots (six each of control, drill-seeded, and connectivity-modifier treatments) in both seasons. For each plot the dataset provides time-synchronized high-resolution forward- and downward-facing RGB imagery, 3D LiDAR point clouds, RTK-corrected GPS, IMU, and LIO-SAM odometry, together with sensor calibration, per-frame GPS and compass-heading uncertainty, and the raw ROS1 recordings. Captured under realistic field conditions (no artificial landmarks, no preplanned paths, extreme visual redundancy, sparse geometric features, and dramatic seasonal change), it is intended to support research in long-term localization and mapping, cross-seasonal data association of individual plants and microsites, and autonomous environmental monitoring in unstructured natural environments where existing cultivated-agriculture datasets are not representative.

title: City-Scale Heat Action Plan (HAP) Content Analysis Dataset: Supporting Data for "An International Assessment of Heat Action Plans"
display_name: City-Scale Heat Action Plan (HAP) Content Analysis Dataset: Supporting Data for "An International Assessment of Heat Action Plans"
abstract: Extreme heat events are rising significantly, posing a growing threat to public health in cities worldwide. Heat Action Plans (HAPs) have emerged as a critical tool for cities to proactively prepare for, manage, and mitigate the impacts of extreme heat. This dataset is part of a study that offers the most comprehensive international assessment of HAPs to date. The project analyzes the content of local government HAPs from around the world and validates the findings with academic and practice-oriented guidance. The study found that cities focus more on heat management strategies than heat mitigation, with emergency preparedness and heat education far outpacing urban greening or waste-heat-reduction measures. The analysis also revealed that heat governance as a third, and previously underemphasized, area of heat action, encompassing: research; planning, policy, and program development; leadership; funding; and community engagement. This dataset includes the list of plans analyzed and the codebook for this study, providing a robust evidence base to inform the next generation of HAPs and equip practitioners with actionable insights to refine and strengthen their design, implementation, and evaluation.

title: Proxies of Natural and Dynamical Variability for the use in Total Column Ozone Trend Studies
display_name: Proxies of Natural and Dynamical Variability for the use in Total Column Ozone Trend Studies
abstract: This dataset provides monthly mean anomaly (Jan 1980-Dec 2025) of derived proxies for dynamical and natural variability for use as explanatory variables in multi-linear regression models in total column ozone trend studies. Trend studies that seek to derive the trend attributable to the reduction in ozone-depleting substances after the Montreal Protocol and its amendments need to account for the ozone variability attributable to other dynamical and natural processes. This dataset, which will be used in such a trend study of Total Column Ozone from the long-term NOAA Total Column Ozone records, makes available several proxies that represent these processes. This includes global proxies of the solar cycle, the quasi-biennial oscillation, El Niño-Southern Oscillation, Arctic Oscillation, the Brewer-Dobson Circulation, and the Antarctic Oscillation. Additionally, short-term variability is modeled through a proxy called the integrated equivalent latitude calculated for each NOAA long-term ozone monitoring station. Finally, a latitudinally resolved aerosol proxy is published here. The resulting dataset offers a way to fit dynamical and natural processes in total column ozone variability so that the resulting derived trend in the multi-linear regression is attributable to the decline in ozone-depleting substances as a result of the international regulations. This dataset is made available under the Creative Commons Zero (CC0 1.0) Universal Public Domain Dedication; the author waives any potential copyright and related rights worldwide. However, Specific data within this publication was derived and modified from the Copernicus Climate Change Service. This includes: The columns qboA and qboB in the file All_others.csv and All data in the file IEQLat.csv. This excepted data retains its original Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) license (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). title: HAZUS-based seismic vulnerability functions for repair cost as a function of SA03
display_name: HAZUS-based seismic vulnerability functions for repair cost as a function of SA03
abstract: These Hazus-based seismic vulnerability functions provide damage factor for 3,584 combinations of Hazus model building type, height class, design level, and occupancy class. Damage factor is expressed in terms of its expected value of its coefficient of variation. Damage factor means repair cost as a fraction of replacement cost new. Damage factors are provided for each of 33 log-spaced increments of 5% damped, 0.3-second spectral accelration response: {0.0, 10^-2.0, 10^-1.9, ... 10^0.9, 10^1.0, 10^2.0} in units of g.

title: SiBCASA-Hg Model Output and Analysis Files for Global Terrestrial Mercury, Carbon, Water, and Energy Cycling, 1901–2025
display_name: SiBCASA-Hg Model Output and Analysis Files for Global Terrestrial Mercury, Carbon, Water, and Energy Cycling, 1901–2025
abstract: This dataset contains model output, processed data, and analysis files associated with the SiBCASA-Hg global land surface model simulation described in the manuscript "SiBCASA-Hg: A Global Land Surface Model of Integrated Mercury, Carbon, Water, and Energy Cycling." SiBCASA-Hg integrates terrestrial mercury cycling with dynamic carbon, water, energy, vegetation, and soil processes. The archived global simulation spans 1901–2025 and includes a historical period (1901–2025). The archive contains model output used to evaluate global and regional carbon and mercury stocks and fluxes, temporal and spatial variability, and comparisons between simulated and observed soil mercury concentrations. It also includes analysis and plotting files used to generate manuscript figures, tables, and quantitative analyses. The SiBCASA-Hg source code and model-run scripts are archived separately on Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22148459. To download this dataset with Globus, follow the link in the Related URLs and follow these instructions. Step 1: Sign in to Globus (https://www.globus.org/app/login). If you are with an institution that is registered with Globus, you can simply sign in with your institutional credentials. If your institution is not registered with Globus, you will need to first make an account (https://www.globusid.org/create) before signing in. Step 2: Install Globus Connect Personal (https://www.globus.org/globus-connect-personal) on your local computer. This will establish your local endpoint to which you can download the CU Scholar dataset. You'll give the local endpoint a name (e.g., "Jane Doe's Laptop") Step 3: Click on the Globus URL for the dataset on its CU Scholar landing page. This will bring up the dataset on the left hand side of the Globus file manager. On the right hand side, search for your endpoint name (e.g., "Jane Doe's Laptop"), which will bring up the file system on your local machine (make sure Globus Connect Personal is running). Highlight the dataset files that you want to transfer and click on the blue "start" button to transfer the data to your machine. Data storage for this dataset is supported by CU Boulder Research Computing's PetaLibrary.

title: SAFRR Tsunami Scenario California Coastal Marina Piling Heights Database
display_name: SAFRR Tsunami Scenario California Coastal Marina Piling Heights Database
abstract: From 2007 through about 2019, the US Geological Survey had an active project called Science Application for Risk Reduction (SAFRR). It aimed to show how USGS science could help US communities better understand, prepare for, and mitigate natural disasters. Among other products, it developed four notable disaster planning scenarios: The ShakeOut scenario (e.g., Porter et al. 2011), ARkStorm Scenario (Porter et al. 2010), Tsuanmi Scenario (Ross et al. 2013), and HayWired Scenario (e.g., Porter 2018). The present work addresses an aspect of the Tsunami Scenario: the potential of a large tsunami to damage boats and marinas along California's coast. A tsunami could potentially lift floating docks in these marinas over the tops of their pilings. To assess the risk of such damage, one must know, among other things, the height of the pilings that prevent docks from lateral movement. In 2013, no database existed of these heights. In collaboration with the USGS, California Geological Survey, and others, I created and exercised a data collection protocol to create such a database. The database reflects almost all California coastal marinas in existance in 2014 through 2016. The work was sponsored by the US Geological Survey under project leader Stephanie L. Ross.

title: HAZUS-based seismic vulnerability functions for repair duration (loss of function) as a function of SA03
display_name: HAZUS-based seismic vulnerability functions for repair duration (loss of function) as a function of SA03
abstract: These Hazus-based seismic vulnerability functions provide repair duration for 3,584 combinations of Hazus model building type, height class, design level, and occupancy class. Repair duration is expressed in terms of its expected value in days. Repair durations are provided for each of 33 log-spaced increments of 5% damped, 0.3-second spectral acceleration response: {0.0, 10^-2.0, 10^-1.9, ... 10^0.9, 10^1.0, 10^2.0} in units of g.

title: Source data for "Motors use biased diffusion to shepherd diffusible proteins on microtubules"
display_name: Source data for "Motors use biased diffusion to shepherd diffusible proteins on microtubules"
abstract: Raw experimental and simulation data for Farhadi, Fiorenza et al., "Motors use biased diffusion to shepherd diffusible proteins on microtubules," Nature Physics (2026). Experimental data are total internal reflection fluorescence (TIRF) microscopy images and timeseries of in vitro reconstitution assays with purified kinesin motors and diffusive microtubule-associated proteins, including kinesin-1 (K401) and PRC1, with the spreadsheets used for plotting. Simulation data are output of stochastic simulations with the CyLaKS software of motors and diffusive MAPs on a multi-protofilament microtubule lattice, with the analysis output used to make the figures. Folders are organized by figure panel. See the README file for details.

title: Datasets associated with "Terpenoids and NOx Drive the Composition of Low Volatility Organic Compounds in the Agricultural Southern Great Plains"
display_name: Datasets associated with "Terpenoids and NOx Drive the Composition of Low Volatility Organic Compounds in the Agricultural Southern Great Plains"
abstract: The associated data products are derived from nitrate anion chemical ionization mass spectrometer measurements made from May 6, 2023 to May 31, 2023 at the Department of Energy (DOE), Atmospheric Radiation Measurement (ARM) Southern Great Plains guest Instrument Facility in Lamont, OK, USA (36.607322 N, 97.487643 W) as part of the "Boundary Layer Gradients in New Particle Formation 2023" campaign (https://armgov.svcs.arm.gov/research/campaigns/sgp2023blnpf). The measurements provide information on the gas-phase molecules that contribute to aerosol growth and mass. The measurements were collected to understand the sources of the compounds that grow newly formed particles to larger sizes. The data deposited here represents derived quantities where individual compounds were grouped according to their volatility classification or the number of hydrogen atoms in the formulas. Individual ion time series can be found at the DOE ARM archive (https://doi.org/10.5439/3683926).

title: Magnetospheric substorm-driven large-amplitude ionospheric bursty prompt penetration electric fields [Dataset]
display_name: Magnetospheric substorm-driven large-amplitude ionospheric bursty prompt penetration electric fields [Dataset]
abstract: Large geomagnetic storms often drive complex upper atmospheric and ionospheric disturbances with a broad range of spatial and temporal scales. We used Jicamarca Radio Observatory observations and complementary solar and geomagnetic field measurements to study the response of equatorial ionospheric electric fields to recent major and moderate geomagnetic storms. Our measurements near dusk and nearly steady southward interplanetary magnetic fields during the 24 April 2023, 10 –11 October 2024, and 16 – 17 May 2025 show very large amplitude (over 100 m/s) short-lived (less than one hour) upward vertical plasma drifts indicative of inductive prompt penetration electric fields. Recent Jicamarca measurements show the occurrence of several additional similar events. We suggest that these large bursty prompt penetration drifts were driven by substorms associated with low entropy magnetospheric bubbles and bursty bulk flows (BBFs). Our data indicate, in particular, that a magnetospheric substorm driven prompt penetration electric field was the main driver of a very large increase of the F layer height over Jicamarca near dusk on 10 October 2024 and of resulting very strong equatorial plasma bubbles extending to mid-latitudes. In this event, the upward drift reached in excess of 300 m/s, corresponding to an eastward electric field of over 7 mV/m, the largest ever observed over Jicamarca. The Jicamarca measurements near dusk during the 16–17 May 2025 moderate magnetic storm show, for the first time, two large amplitude, short lived, substorm-associated, bursty prompt penetration drifts near dusk driving strong equatorial plasma irregularities. The early night large amplitude prompt perturbation drifts during these storms are not reproduced by widely used Prompt Penetration Electric Field Model (PPEFM). Ours and complementary observations highlight both the complex response of the low latitude ionosphere to geomagnetic storms and the need for more extensive high time resolution global measurements for their better understanding.

title: Mountain Research Station Tundra Laboratory Site: Water vapor Isotope Measurements along the Colorado Front Range
display_name: Mountain Research Station Tundra Laboratory Site: Water vapor Isotope Measurements along the Colorado Front Range
abstract: Data in this set represent nearly continuous measurements of water vapor and heavy water isotopologues taken between January and July 2025 as part of the Picarro Front Range Experiment (PIFREX). Water-vapor isotopes provide a tracer of atmospheric moisture sources, transport, and local hydrological processes, but separating variability across spatial and temporal scales remains challenging. PIFREX present an eight-month record of continuous water-vapor isotope measurements 3 sites along the Colorado Front Range at elevations from ~1600 to 3500 m along am about 30 km transect. A dataset Readme is included along with the data in the downloadable zip file.
